==Māori==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|mi|poz-pol-pro|*kawa}} (cognates include {{cog|haw|ʻawa}}, {{cog|to|kava}} and {{cog|sm|ʻava}})<ref>{{R:mi:Tregear:1891|page=139}}</ref><ref>{{cite-web|titleurl=https://www.temarareo.org/TMR-Kawa.html|title=Kawa, Kawakawa|year=2023|site=Te Māra Reo|publisher=Benson Family Trust}}
</ref> from {{inh|mi|poz-oce-pro|*kawaʀ||potent root}} metathesis of {{inh|mi|poz-oce-pro|*wakaʀ||root}}, thus {{doublet|mi|aka|nocap=1}}. Sense of plant lost with species introduced to Aotearoa dying out due to its cold climate.<ref>{{cite book|first=Terry|last=Crowley|last3=Ross |first3=Malcolm |last2=Pawley |first2=Andrew|year=1994|chapter=Proto who drank kava?|title=Austronesian terminologies: Continuity and change|page=95|location=Canberra|publisher=Dept. of Linguistics, Research School
of Pacific and Asian Studies, The Australian National University}}</ref> Sense of "marae protocol" seems to be a modern extension.

===Pronunciation===
* {{mi-IPA|kawa|stress='-}}

===Adjective===
{{mi-adj}}

# [[sour]]

===Noun===
{{mi-noun}}

# {{non-gloss|a ceremony to remove {{l|mi|tapu}} from a new house or canoe}}
# {{non-gloss|{{l|mi|karakia|t=ritual chants}} and customs for the opening of new houses, canoes and other events}}
# [[marae]] [[protocol]] - {{non-gloss|customs of the marae and {{l|mi|wharenui}}, particularly those related to formal activities such as {{l|mi|pōhiri}}, speeches and {{l|mi|mihimihi}}}}
# [[acid]]
# [[bitterness]]
# {{lb|mi|obsolete}} [[kava]], plant brought by ancestors from the South Pacific, {{taxfmt|Piper methysticum|species}}.

====Descendants====
* {{desc|en|kawa|bor=1}}

===Verb===
{{mi-verb}}

# {{non-gloss|to perform the kawa ceremony, open a new house}}

* {{l|mi|kawanga}}

===Related terms===
* {{l|mi|kawakawa}}
